newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines eyes sites for nuclear power plant.
newsitem.headline: Philippines eyes sites for nuclear power plant.

text.p: The Philippines Department of Energy said on Wednesday it has identified ten possible sites for a nuclear power plant.

Energy Secretary Francisco Viray said in an initial feasibility report submitted to President Fidel Ramos that five of the sites are on the northern island of Luzon, three are on the central Visayas island and two on the southern island of Mindanao.
The energy official said the sites are situated far from active volcanoes and populated areas.
The country's 30-year Power Development Programme, covering the years 1996 to 2025, provides for a nuclear power plant to be set up by 2025.

There is no nuclear power plant in operation in the Philippines. A 620-megawatt nuclear power plant in Bataan, north of Manila, was built in the 1980s but was never commissioned due to a legal battle between the government and the builders of the plant, Westinghouse Electric Corp and Burns & Roe.
The state-owned National Power Corp is planning to convert the plant into a gas-fired power plant.
